name: Habiganj
tagline: Sylhet's quiet corner — rainforest gibbons, lotus lakes in the tea hills, and a 16th-century Sultanate mosque.

guide.bestTime: October to March (cool, dry; forests and tea gardens at their best)
guide.gettingThere: By road from Dhaka (~210 km, ~4–5 hr) on the Dhaka–Sylhet highway, or by rail to Shaistaganj Junction on the Dhaka–Sylhet line. The forests and lakes lie in Chunarughat and Madhabpur, 30–60 km south of town.
guide.difficulty: Easy to moderate — town and tea gardens are easy; the forest trails of Rema-Kalenga and Satchari need a guide and some walking.

mustVisit.name: Satchari National Park
mustVisit.description: A compact tropical rainforest on Raghunandan hill in Chunarughat, ringed by tea gardens. Its name means 'seven streams.' Short forest trails give you a real chance of hearing — and sometimes seeing — the endangered hoolock gibbon.
mustVisit.history: Declared a national park in 2005, covering about 243 hectares of the larger Raghunandan reserve forest. Home to hoolock gibbons, capped langurs, pythons and a rich bird community; a Tipra (Tripura) Adivasi settlement sits inside the forest.

practical.hours: Daytime; early morning is best for gibbons and birds

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 60 km south of Habiganj town, off the Dhaka–Sylhet highway in Chunarughat
howToReach.transport: Bus toward Chunarughat / Satchari, then a short walk to the forest gate

mustVisit.bestTime: October to March; arrive at dawn for wildlife
tips: Hire a Forest Department guide at the gate for the trails and gibbon spotting
Wear closed shoes and long sleeves — leeches appear after rain
Keep quiet on the trail; gibbons move off at noise

mustVisit.name: Rema-Kalenga Wildlife Sanctuary
mustVisit.description: One of the oldest and largest surviving natural forests in Bangladesh, deep in Chunarughat — far quieter and wilder than Satchari, with watchtowers, mixed evergreen hills and a long species list.
mustVisit.history: A wildlife sanctuary of roughly 1,795 hectares holding endangered hoolock gibbons and leopards among some 37 mammal, 167 bird, 18 reptile and 638 plant species recorded in the forest.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 60–70 km southeast of Habiganj town in Chunarughat, beyond Satchari
howToReach.transport: Bus or hired vehicle to Kalenga via Chunarughat; the last stretch is rough road

tips: A guide is essential — the trails are long and easy to lose
Start early; it is a half-day round trip from the road
Carry water and food; there are no shops in the forest

mustVisit.name: Shankarpasha Shahi Mosque
mustVisit.description: A rare surviving Sultanate-era mosque at Uchail Shankarpasha — a single-domed brick mosque with terracotta detailing that has stood for over five centuries.
mustVisit.history: Completed in 1513 during the reign of Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah, in memory of the saint Shah Majlis-e-Amin. It stands in Uchail Shankarpasha village of Rajiura Union, Habiganj Sadar, and is protected as an archaeological monument.

practical.hours: Open around the five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 8 km from Habiganj town, in Rajiura Union

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon light on the brickwork
tips: Avoid Friday noon prayers unless you intend to pray
Cover head if female; remove shoes before entering

mustVisit.name: Komola Rani'r Dighi (Sagar Dighi)
mustVisit.description: A vast historic tank in Baniachong wrapped in legend — the great pond at the heart of what is often called the largest village in Asia.
mustVisit.history: Said to have been excavated around the 12th century by a king named Padmanabh. Legend holds that the tank stayed dry until the king's wife, Queen Kamala, sacrificed herself in its waters — a story the poet Jasimuddin retold in verse.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 12 km north of Habiganj town, in Baniachong

tips: Combine with a walk through Baniachong, said to be Asia's biggest village
The banks are unfenced — mind the edges

mustVisit.name: Bithangal Akhra
mustVisit.description: A roughly 600-year-old Vaishnava akhra (monastic shrine) set among the haor wetlands of Baniachong — a remote, atmospheric pilgrimage site reached largely by boat.
mustVisit.history: An old centre of Vaishnava devotion among the antiquities of Baniachong, alongside Komola Rani'r Dighi and Lakshmi Baor. It draws devotees for its festivals and is best reached by boat across the haor.

practical.hours: Daytime; access depends on the season and water level

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: North of Habiganj near Baniachong; by jeep to Sujatpur in the dry season or by boat across the haor in the rains
howToReach.transport: Boat from Baniachong Adarsha Bazar or Habiganj Kalar Duba; jeep in the dry season

mustVisit.bestTime: Dry season for road access; monsoon for the full haor boat journey
tips: Confirm the water level locally before setting out — the route changes with the season
Respect ongoing worship at the akhra

specialties.name: Habiganj Estate Tea
specialties.description: Habiganj is a tea district — Chunarughat, Madhabpur and Bahubal are dotted with estates. A glass of fresh, strong garden tea is the local drink of choice.
specialties.venue: Tea-garden canteens and town tea stalls

specialties.name: Shatkora Beef
specialties.description: The hallmark greater-Sylhet dish — beef slow-cooked with shatkora, a fragrant local citrus that gives the gravy a distinctive bittersweet edge.

bucketlist.title: Listen for hoolock gibbons in Satchari at dawn
bucketlist.detail: The gibbons call across the canopy in the first hour of light. Walk the 'seven streams' trail with a Forest Department guide for the best chance of hearing — and glimpsing — them.

bucketlist.title: Trek deep into Rema-Kalenga
bucketlist.detail: One of the country's oldest and largest natural forests — watchtowers, hill trails and a species list that runs to hundreds of birds and plants. Wilder and quieter than Satchari.

bucketlist.title: Visit the 1513 Shankarpasha Shahi Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A single-domed Sultanate-era mosque that has stood for over five centuries — one of the oldest surviving mosques in the region.

bucketlist.title: Walk the banks of Komola Rani'r Dighi
bucketlist.detail: A vast historic tank wrapped in the legend of a queen who gave her life so it would fill with water — a story the poet Jasimuddin set in verse.

bucketlist.title: Stand in Baniachong — said to be Asia's largest village
bucketlist.detail: Endless homesteads, ponds and paddy stretching to the horizon. Pair it with the dighi and the nearby Bithangal Akhra.

bucketlist.title: Take a haor boat to Bithangal Akhra
bucketlist.detail: A 600-year-old Vaishnava shrine reached across the wetlands. In the monsoon the boat journey through the haor is the experience in itself.
bucketlist.bestTime: Monsoon for the full boat journey

bucketlist.title: Drink fresh estate tea in a Chunarughat garden
bucketlist.detail: Habiganj is tea country. A glass of strong, fresh garden tea, with the rows of bushes climbing the hills around you, is the simplest local pleasure.

bucketlist.title: Eat shatkora beef, the greater-Sylhet way
bucketlist.detail: Beef slow-cooked with shatkora — a fragrant local citrus that gives the gravy its signature bittersweet bite.

bucketlist.title: Find Bipin Chandra Pal's village at Poil
bucketlist.detail: The birthplace of one third of the 'Lal Bal Pal' trio that drove the Swadeshi movement — a quiet pilgrimage for anyone interested in the subcontinent's freedom struggle.

foods.name: Habiganj Estate Tea
foods.description: Fresh, strong tea from the district's many gardens in Chunarughat, Madhabpur and Bahubal — the everyday local drink.

foods.name: Shatkora Beef
foods.description: The hallmark greater-Sylhet dish — beef cooked with shatkora citrus for a distinctive bittersweet gravy.

foods.name: Akhni (Sylheti Pulao)
foods.description: The Sylheti take on a spiced meat-and-rice pulao, fragrant with whole spices — a feast-day staple across the region.

famousPeople.name: Bipin Chandra Pal
famousPeople.knownFor: Nationalist leader, orator and writer — one third of the 'Lal Bal Pal' triumvirate and a key architect of the Swadeshi movement. Born in Poil village, Habiganj.

famousPeople.name: Dewan Farid Gazi
famousPeople.knownFor: Politician from Nabiganj and a civil-affairs advisor to Mukti Bahini sectors 3 and 4 during the 1971 Liberation War; later a long-serving member of parliament for Habiganj.

didYouKnow: Baniachong in Habiganj is often described as the largest village in Asia by area and population.
Bipin Chandra Pal — one third of the 'Lal Bal Pal' trio that drove the Swadeshi movement — was born in Poil village, Habiganj, in 1858.
Shankarpasha Shahi Mosque was completed in 1513 under Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah — a rare surviving Sultanate-era mosque with over five centuries of heritage.
Rema-Kalenga is one of Bangladesh's oldest and largest natural forests, home to the endangered hoolock gibbon and hundreds of bird and plant species.
Satchari — 'seven streams' — National Park sits on Raghunandan hill amid nine tea gardens in Chunarughat, with a Tipra Adivasi village inside the forest.
The legend of Komola Rani'r Dighi in Baniachong — a queen who is said to have drowned herself so the great tank would fill with water — inspired a poem by Jasimuddin.
